correctness.rationale: For affine disks, the Fourier-energy density becomes radial after the affine change of variables, so the double-Hilbert defect is exactly the angular fraction of same-sign or opposite-sign quadrants; this yields the closed all-ellipse formula and the log-free diagonal-ellipse rate. For the published truncated strip, the exact source integral has tail A(t)=1/(2t)+O(t^-2), producing the claimed epsilon^2 log(1/epsilon) leading term with all normalization factors checked.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The full recent source arXiv:2609.15155v1 was checked around its continuous quasi-eigenvector construction and contains the truncated-strip upper bound but no ellipse construction, all-ellipse exact defect identity, or matching strip asymptotic. Exact and synonymous literature searches and the current SCOPE archive produced no matching theorem. An older inaccessible Patel paper was checked at the abstract level and concerns polynomial-surface Lp boundedness, not indicator quasi-eigenvectors. Because the source preprint is very recent and the ellipse calculation is concise, unindexed concurrent or folklore observation remains possible.

value.rationale: The result separates two phenomena that the recent paper leaves conflated: the logarithm is sharp for its hard truncated strip, yet is not intrinsic to bounded continuous quasi-eigenvectors. Smooth strictly convex ellipses give an exact log-free square-root defect, and the all-ellipse formula identifies the controlling geometric angle explicitly.
